title: Rendering, preview and analysis
objective: Keep the one render pipeline and make it smaller, faster and easier to test: a render context per test, one home for limits, a trimmed pixel-domain trait, byte-identical speedups on the tile, frame, resample, threshold, point and proxy paths, a drafted preview that skips work nobody sees, an exact viewport-region path with a half-scale interactive preview, opaque frames, render.rs split by concept and one test per property, then stage-boundary methods before Corrections adds a new boundary.
context_summary: Rendering has one entry point (luxforge_core::render) with an injected RenderContext, one latest-job worker, one tile function and one point pipeline generic over the byte and linear pixel domains, so a sample equals the rendered byte by construction. The domain unification left a 23-item PixelDomain trait with about ten one-sided items, three separate copies of the resample read-rectangle and two of spatial-entry orchestration in the frame drivers, and a one-megapixel parallel threshold declared five times across two crates, beside a separate 256 Ki heavy-colour threshold that a colour pass with at least three units or a mask uses while every other pass keeps the one-megapixel one. The pipeline also leaves the pool idle during serial tile write-back and frame zeroing, and spends three power-function calls per pixel quantizing the byte resample. Every task keeps renders and samples byte-identical and measures its effect before claiming it; the owner's decisions and the programme's constraints are recorded in docs/decisions.md and docs/design/post-consolidation.md. The viewport design, accepted softness/histogram tradeoff and viewport-bounded clipping behavior are implemented in the current worktree. Half-scale interactive regions use exact whole-stage estimates from the shared eight-entry cache; sampled reduced guides are rejected because periodic inputs alias. Prior native evidence remains scoped to its recorded builds. On the final review release binary, quick and rendered (33 native smoke scenarios) passed; three permanent viewport journeys recorded zero blank or stale photo draws, and 16 targeted timing cases completed. No post-review full-tier result or milestone qualification is claimed. The original moving-frame RAW white-balance gate missed on the Air 2S at 17.33% against 10%; the owner revised the 100% gate on 2026-09-27 to test the held full-detail draft after quiet refinement. Fresh native `raw-panel` runs pass for all three supplied cameras under the revised gate. The 1088 MiB temporary photo-texture overlap ceiling is provisionally accepted for those slots only; crop GPU textures, overlays and backend staging remain outside it and are not fully measured or bounded. No total-memory guarantee or general numerical photo-error bound is qualified.

tasks.description: Give every core unit test that renders its own RenderContext, deleting the shared static test context, its guards and its idle polls.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. A render context per test removes the mechanism behind a class of load-dependent test failures, before the harness states the rule that depends on it.

`render::testing::context()` (render.rs:1725-1728) is a `static OnceLock<RenderContext>` that every `render::testing` helper (`render`, `render_tiled`, `render_cancellable`, `render_proxy_cancellable`, the linear equivalents, `sample`) renders through, reached directly or through those helpers from 9 files. Tests serialise on `scratch_guard` (23 call sites) and `spatial_guard` (40 call sites), reset the shared estimate store with `clear_estimates()` (51 call sites across 4 files), and poll the shared budget until it drains before asserting exact in-use, peak or estimate counts.

`set_target` and `reset_peak` on `RenderContext` (render/context.rs:125, 205, 223) are `pub` only because tests mutate the shared context's budget target directly, including lowering it to 0 while other tests render through the same context on other threads: the comment beside one such test says exactly that ('other tests' preview workers reserve from it on their own threads').

`RenderContext::new()` is already cheap, and three call sites (preview/tests.rs:582, analysis/jobs.rs:877, resources.rs:244) already build their own context instead of sharing the static one; this task generalises what they already do to every test.

This is the same shape of failure as a recorded flake in the RAW crate's own scratch-permit test: a count that depends on what else the test binary happens to be running concurrently, because both share process-wide state across parallel test threads.

tasks.description: Declare the parallel thresholds, the 512 MiB frame limit, the side limit and the spatial tile size once, in a limits module the core and the RAW crate both import.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. Every speedup later in this group tunes a threshold; each should tune one declaration, not several.

The 1 MP threshold is declared five times: `PARALLEL_RENDER_PIXELS` (render.rs:40), `PARALLEL_PROXY_PIXELS` (proxy.rs:27), `PARALLEL_CAMERA_PIXELS` (source.rs:228), `PARALLEL_REDUCE_PIXELS` (analysis.rs:34, whose own comment says it mirrors `render::PARALLEL_RENDER_PIXELS`) and `PARALLEL_CORRECTION_PIXELS` (luxforge-raw/src/dng.rs:20); `PARALLEL_GRID_CELLS` (analysis/mask_overlay.rs:80) aliases the analysis copy. `PARALLEL_HEAVY_COLOUR_PIXELS` (256 Ki, render.rs:43), which the colour pass uses for a heavy pass (render/pipeline.rs:795-806), is a second parallel threshold and belongs in the same module.

The 512 MiB frame limit has three production spellings: `FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES` (proxy.rs:31), `MAX_RGBA_BYTES` (render/linear.rs:25) and a bare `512 * 1024 * 1024` comparison in `Raster::expected_len` (render.rs:462). A fourth copy survives only in the test-only `previous_decode` bench in source.rs's tests (the `image` reader's `max_alloc`), which imports the constant or is exempt from the rule. render/spatial.rs's `PRODUCTION_TILE` (render/spatial.rs:1152) is only an alias of `SPATIAL_TILE` (modules/spatial.rs:16). The 16384 px side limit has three copies: `luxforge_raw::MAX_SIDE` (luxforge-raw/src/limits.rs:7), render/linear.rs's own `MAX_SIDE` (render/linear.rs:23), which sits beside constants the same file already derives from luxforge_raw, and `JPEG_LIMITS.max_side` (source.rs:28-31); the last two use the shared constant. Decide in the change whether `REGION_FRAME_BYTES` (32 MiB viewport frame, render/entry.rs:149) and `MAX_JPEG_BYTES` (source.rs:24) join the module.

luxforge-raw already has a limits module (crates/luxforge-raw/src/limits.rs) that the core imports `MAX_PIXELS`, `MAX_RGB_BYTES`, `MAX_SIDE` and `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` from; the shared constants belong there, or in a small module both crates depend on, following that existing pattern rather than a new one. `luxforge-jpeg` declares no limit values, only the `Limits` struct the core fills, and may depend on no workspace crate (`cargo xtask check-repository` enforces it), so the limits module does not span it.

The repository rule is scoped so it does not flag values that only share a spelling: `FULL_BUDGET` (luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs:92) is a GPU texture budget and luxforge-raw's `MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` (luxforge-raw/src/limits.rs:3) bounds source-file bytes, both 512 MiB. The rule matches declarations in the core and RAW crates' sources outside the limits module, or exempts those two by name.
Every value stays what it is today, only declared once, so renders and samples are unaffected by this task on their own.

tasks.description: Trim the pixel-domain pipeline to one resample read-rectangle rule and one spatial-entry helper, delete the GRID policy knob, and move the domain-independent no-op checks into Render.
extra_context: Wave 2, finish the consolidation. The generic pipeline is the right design; it should describe only what the two domains actually do differently.

`PixelDomain` (render/pipeline.rs:52-166) has 23 items: 3 associated types, 1 const and 19 methods. About ten are no-ops, identities or unreachable on one side: `Byte::frame_pixel` (render.rs:1323) is never called because Byte's `GRID` is `SpatialMode::Point` (render.rs:1186) while Linear's is `SpatialMode::Frames` (render/linear.rs:640), so a grid is materialised for one domain and tiled for the other. `Linear::adjust_source_pixel` (render/linear.rs:620-631) is an identity on every exact evaluation, a white-balance multiply only under an approximate white balance, and repeats the finiteness check `pixel_f64` (render/linear.rs:377-390) has already made; it is another one-sided item to trim.

The rectangle a resample reads is computed three separate ways, each with its own margin: `rows_read_by` (render.rs:711, -2/+3 rows), the proxy window's `tap_region` (render/window.rs:145, `TAP_MARGIN` 2) and a second `tap_region` (render/linear.rs:979, -1/+2 clamped, capped at `TAP_BLOCK_PIXELS`). Resamples carry an output window: `Segment::entry_window` (render.rs:847), `resample_output_at` (render.rs:870) and the windowed `resample_frame`. The one rule, `Resample::reads`, takes the entry origin and the output window and uses one margin that covers all three. `WindowPlan::of_rect` (render/window.rs:202-268) is a separate halo and tile-alignment rule, out of scope, and the one-home check does not trip on it. Spatial-entry orchestration (resolve or reuse handed globals, reduce, call `spatial_output`) is written out twice: inline in the byte driver (render.rs:1655-1695) and as `Evaluation::spatial_globals` (render/pipeline.rs:514-541, called from the `spatial_output` call at render/pipeline.rs:251).

The 8x8 capability sample grid (capabilities/data.rs, `SampleGrid8`) reads 64 points through `grid_in` (render/entry.rs:751-768), which evaluates in `D::GRID` mode (render/entry.rs:759); because `GRID` is `Frames` for the linear domain, a RAW asset with a spatial layer materialises a full spatial frame to answer it, where the byte domain answers the same 64 points by reading tiles.

Alpha handling, `bilinear`'s blend (render.rs:397-427) and `alpha_in` (render/pipeline.rs:589), is left to TASK-013, which deletes it with opaque frames. The two rendering-unification commits added roughly 250 net production lines rather than removing them; this is where that count comes back down. Constraint: renders and samples stay byte-identical on both domains, since the read rectangles being unified are supersets of what each domain reads today, and a windowed downscale already proves equal to the whole one inside it.

tasks.description: Write each spatial tile's batch back with per-row copy_from_slice, produced in the frame's final layout during the parallel phase, instead of copying one pixel at a time on the calling thread.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. The clearest byte-identical win in the group: the same values move to the same places, only as whole rows instead of one pixel at a time.

`run_batches` (render/spatial.rs:605) evaluates a batch in parallel and then writes it back serially (render/spatial.rs:636): `for (tile, result) in batch.iter().zip(results) { write(*tile, result)?; }`. `Byte::write_tile` (render.rs:1305) copies three bytes and calls an alpha closure per pixel; `Linear::write_tile` (render/linear.rs:813) does the planar equivalent. The pool sits idle during every one of these writes.

Recorded CPU utilisation on the generated fixtures matches a serial write of this size: Clarity at 60 MP renders in 620 ms at 1105% CPU (about 140 ms serial-equivalent), Dehaze in 355 ms at 713% (about 190 ms), Texture in 629 ms at 858% (about 260 ms); the 24 MP figures (193 ms at 1090%, 128 ms at 771%) scale down consistently (docs/specs/performance.md, Presence exact renders on the generated JPEGs).

Proposal: have tile_output (already computed in the parallel phase) produce the tile in the frame's final row layout, then have write_tile copy whole rows with copy_from_slice, one memcpy per row for the byte frame's RGBA rows and three for the linear frame's planes, instead of a per-pixel loop; reuse one scratch buffer per worker in run_tile rather than reallocating and zero-filling it per tile.

tasks.description: Allocate frames as Arc<Vec<u8>> from vec![0; n] instead of a serial byte-by-byte fill, and copy an identity segment's source rows inside the parallel pass instead of up front on one thread.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Pairs with the tile write-back speedup: both remove a serial full-frame pass that the parallel pass then overwrites anyway.

`zeroed_frame` (render.rs:484) is `std::iter::repeat_n(0, len).collect::<Arc<[u8]>>()`, which writes every byte serially on the calling thread: 96 MB at 24 MP, 240 MB at 60 MP, 159 MB for the X100VI's RAW output. Its callers include the resample, a non-identity segment, the byte spatial frame, the RAW linear output, the proxy, `SourceImage::window` (source.rs:65) and JPEG decode, which zero-fills the frame before libjpeg writes every row into it (source.rs:165). An identity segment with a colour run additionally copies the whole source up front with `Arc::<[u8]>::from(source.rgba.as_ref())` (render.rs:1718) before the parallel colour pass runs.

Proposal: hold frames as Arc<Vec<u8>> allocated with vec![0; len] (fresh pages are already zero and are faulted in by whichever worker first writes them), as LinearImage already holds its planes in Arc<Vec<f32>>. For the identity-with-colour case, let the row loader copy source rows inside the parallel pass, with a row copy_from_slice fast path when the geometry is the identity, instead of copying the whole source first.

This changes the field type of two pub fields on Raster and SourceImage; the desktop and presenter (Frame::new, luxforge-ui/src/photo_surface.rs:157) accept anything implementing AsRef<[u8]>, so a thin wrapper keeps them unchanged. Current shapes only: this is an internal type change, not a catalog or API one.

tasks.description: Quantize the byte resample's bilinear sample through the guarded threshold lookup the RAW terminal already uses, and remove per-pixel LazyLock dereferences and view-layout recomputation from the hot colour and RAW read loops.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. A straightened crop's resample is the largest per-pixel cost left on the gesture path it serves.

`bilinear` (render.rs:397) quantizes each of a pixel's three channels with `linear_to_srgb` (colour.rs:155), which calls the sRGB encode power function once per channel: three powf calls per output pixel. `quantize_channel` (colour.rs:134), used elsewhere, already answers the same question through a guarded lookup (`CODE_INDEX`/`CODE_THRESHOLDS`) with no power function per pixel, and the RAW terminal path already relies on that same guard argument. A 24 MP 10-degree crop outputs about 7.7 MP, so this is roughly 23 million powf calls; instant-preview.md records the straightened crop adding about 30 ms to a 24 MP exact render and about 23 ms to the proxy frame.

Smaller costs in the same loops: `decode_pixel` and `quantize_channel` dereference a LazyLock table on every call, an atomic load the compiler cannot merge, up to six times per pixel across the byte colour path. `LinearImage::pixel` (render/linear.rs:358) recomputes `output_dimensions()`, `view.map()` and a plane-length `try_from` on every call. Frame renders already read through a precomputed `ViewReader` (render/linear.rs:394); the point path (`source_pixel` through `pixel_f64`) still pays the recomputation per pixel, and `pixel_f64` re-checks finiteness that construction already proved. The finiteness scan after each colour unit (render.rs:324) short-circuits with `all(...)`, which cannot vectorise.

Constraint: byte identity for the resample change rests on the same guard the RAW terminal already ships with, not on construction alone; extend the existing boundary tests to linear_to_srgb and prove it with full-frame hashes of rotated-crop renders, not only the boundary cases.

tasks.description: Choose each rendering pass's parallel threshold from its measured work per pixel instead of the one one-megapixel constant, so small proxies of heavy stacks still use the pool.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. A heavy colour pass already uses the shared pool from 256 Ki pixels when it contains at least three units or a mask (docs/engineering/performance-rules.md Rule 9); what remains is the transform, resample, spatial and proxy passes, which keep the one-megapixel threshold.

This is a per-pass threshold decision for the remaining passes, each measured before it changes. Do not claim that all work below one megapixel is serial. RAW Exposure is a Basic colour operation and counts toward the heavy-colour gate (render/pipeline.rs:795-804), so per-pass measurements use current recipes.
Viewport performance evidence uses the native Fit and zoomed scenarios in docs/specs/performance.md. Loaded runs are labeled with their host load and are not treated as clean-load qualification.

tasks.description: Read tile rows instead of one pixel at a time for point queries through a spatial segment and for the global-estimate reduction that feeds units such as Dehaze.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. The row reader this task uses already exists and already proves equal to the per-pixel path; this closes the two pulls the domain unification left per-pixel.

`PointTiles::pixel` (render/spatial.rs:783) fills a tile's input region one pixel at a time through the pipeline's `spatial_read` -> `pixel_in`. The global-estimate reduction (render/pipeline.rs and render/spatial.rs's `build_reduction` / `build_reduction_by_tiles`) reads every pixel of the stage the same way, and the byte domain's `colour_row` falls back to `PixelDomain`'s per-pixel default rather than a row implementation. `Evaluation::fill_rows` (render/pipeline.rs:453) and the row-equals-point contract it already proves are used only by linear frame renders today.

On RAW, the Dehaze global estimate is keyed by `{prefix}+linear:{development}:{view}` plus the approximate white-balance key when there is one (render/linear.rs:652-665). Exposure is a Basic layer in the recipe prefix, so the estimate is rebuilt on every upstream edit and, during a Basic drag, on every input frame. Estimated from the per-pixel cost (not yet a recorded RAW-with-Dehaze drag measurement): the X100VI's 40 MP exact-phase reduction is on the order of 4-5 s of CPU, about 0.3-0.4 s wall, and a 1.65 MP RAW proxy on the order of 190 ms of CPU, about 14 ms wall, per drag frame. The byte path does not pay this, because it reads its already-materialized frame instead.

Proposal: give PointTiles::pixel and the reduction builders a region fetch backed by Evaluation::fill_rows, implement Byte::colour_row with the row arithmetic ByteRows::run already uses, and delete the per-pixel read closures; block_mean keeps summing in the same order so estimates stay identical.

tasks.description: Build the proxy's box downscale in row bands instead of one full-window float intermediate, compile the proxy stage once per job instead of twice, and drop the previous cached proxy before building its replacement.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Three independent proxy-build costs the design already bounds in principle but the code does not yet honour.

`BoxDownscale::new` (proxy.rs:488) allocates one intermediate of window width x every source row the window reads x 3 f32 before its vertical pass runs: 124 MiB for a 24 MP JPEG proxy, 159 MiB for the X100VI, 198 MiB at 60 MP, all at the owner's 2880x1800 display bound. instant-preview.md says the proxy adds at most one bounded buffer; this one scales with the source instead.

`proxy_window` (render/entry.rs:596) compiles the proxy stage and computes `WindowPlan::of`, and `render_proxy` (render/entry.rs:634) compiles and plans again and, for a Byte source, re-runs the source check; a job with a proxy phase compiles its stack more than once per stage. The existing test named for that claim, `a_preview_job_compiles_its_stack_once_per_stage_it_renders_at` (preview/tests.rs:741), counts only calls to `render()`, so it does not see the window-plan compile inside `proxy_window`.
The previous cached proxy (preview/worker.rs, proxy.rs's cache insert) stays alive for the whole build of its replacement, on top of the new intermediate.

Proposal: stream the vertical pass in row bands (about 1 MiB per worker instead of the whole window), each band reading only the source rows it needs with one row of overlap between bands; let proxy_window hand its compiled stage and WindowPlan back for render_proxy to reuse; clear the cache entry before building the replacement.

tasks.description: Qualify the drafted-job exact-phase deferral at Fit and record its effect on paint/drag latency and the shared 120 ms quiet policy.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. This measurement is ordered before the masking group's own paint-latency work, so that work can attribute its figures correctly.

Before exact-phase deferral, every Fit preview job rendered its full-resolution exact phase and each drafted request asked for `.analyse()` after the proxy (`crates/luxforge-app/src/app/tasks.rs`, `draft_set_now`; `crates/luxforge-core/src/preview/worker.rs`). During moving input that exact work was often superseded before adoption and could delay the next interactive frame. The baseline preview request-to-worker-start was 6.6/18.2 ms (p50/p95; docs/specs/performance.md, “Bare recipe at photo size”).

The release's commit refresh already renders the exact frame and histogram once the gesture stops, so withholding the drafted exact phase at Fit loses nothing a released frame does not already provide.

The 120 ms exact-phase deferral is implemented for Fit drafts. Compare editor-latency --mode paint and --mode drag with before measurements; report the measured result either way and retain exact report adoption after quiet/release.

The shared pause policy also serves viewport refinement: latest accepted input drained, no pending input, draft round trip or commit, then a measured quiet interval without gesture or view motion. The shared interval is 120 ms, driven by the single 25 ms quiet timer; this task records its latency effect and verifies that the timer is disarmed after settlement. Release bypasses the interval after draining its final input, resumed motion supersedes refinement, and settled idle leaves no timer armed. Do not introduce a separate viewport timeout.

tasks.description: Decide whether a spatial operation with a large summed halo runs in larger tiles, so Texture and Dehaze stop recomputing the margin Clarity needs around every tile.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Blocked on the owner's decision; measured, not implemented.

A render the spatial target holds to fewer tiles than the pool has workers already spreads each tile's passes over the pool, so a 60 MP render with all three Presence fields uses about twelve cores and takes about 3.4 s. What remains is work repeated in the halo: in 512 px tiles Dehaze computes 5.2 times the stage and Texture 4.9 times, because each tile carries Clarity's 327 px halo, and the render spends about twice the CPU time it did when two tiles ran with serial passes.

Measured with 1024 px tiles and pooled passes on the generated 60 MP JPEG (5 samples, load 8 to 12): all three fields 2.09 s against 3.67 s in 512 px tiles on the same run, Texture and Clarity 1.62 s against 2.63 s, with total CPU time back to the serial-pass figure. One tile's working set is then 208.5 MiB, so batches hold one tile inside the 256 MiB target. The frame was byte-identical to the 512 px render for Texture with Clarity and for all three fields on the 24 MP and 60 MP fixtures.

Samples through a spatial layer are now answered by a dedicated point worker, off the catalog owner, so a larger tile costs only the sampling client its own wait, not every other client: the pointer readout goes from 104 to 107 ms to 217 to 218 ms with all three fields at 60 MP, and from 13 to 50 ms with Texture alone (9 interior points, each equal to the rendered byte), but no longer delays another client's request the way it would when sampling ran on the owner. Byte identity across tile sizes is asserted by tests and holds on these fixtures, but the box passes' running sums start at each rectangle's edge, so it rests on evidence rather than construction.
A tile size chosen from the summed halo (512 px for a small one, 1024 px once it passes some bound) would keep samples through a small-halo stack as cheap as today.

tasks.description: Declare every frame opaque RGBA and delete alpha blending, fetching and threading from the render paths.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Follows the frame-allocation change so the byte tile write can become a plain row copy with no per-pixel alpha read.

Owner decision: frames are opaque by contract. Every production byte frame already is: JPEG decode takes libjpeg's RGBA output (luxforge-jpeg's decode.rs, `header.rgba()`), whose alpha is always 255, the proxy (proxy.rs) writes 255, and analysis.rs already documents that the supported JPEG path is opaque.

Despite that, the renderer still blends alpha through resamples (`bilinear`'s alpha average, reached through the windowed `resample_frame`), walks the geometry to fetch a spatial output's input alpha (`alpha_in`, render/pipeline.rs), and threads an alpha closure through `spatial_output` and `write_tile`. It is also inconsistent: the exact path preserves a source's alpha while the proxy discards it, so 'proxy equals the exact recipe over the exact downscale' would not hold for a hypothetical non-opaque source, harmless only because none exists.
Test fixtures with varying alpha (the gradient source builder in render.rs, and `samples_match_rendered_pixels_and_keep_source_alpha` at render.rs:3801) become uniformly opaque.

tasks.description: Split render.rs by concept into separate files with no logic change, and fold in shared region and segment constructors, one Cancel module, LinearImage beside SourceImage, and the small clean-ups listed below.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Landed last among the render changes so the split starts from the final shape, not one later tasks would immediately move again.

render.rs is 5,582 lines, 1,686 of them production, mixing about eleven concepts: Cancel, colour runs, the bilinear resample, Raster and frame helpers, exact geometry and the resample mapping, the compiled IR (Entry / Segment / Compiled), the public locate and transform types, the Byte domain, ByteRows, LayerInput / grid_centres / stage_transform, and the byte driver. Cancel is the crate's general cancellation token, used by latest, analysis and the capability jobs, not only by rendering.
render/linear.rs holds LinearImage, the RAW source's own data type, while the JPEG source type SourceImage lives in source.rs; the two peer types are asymmetrically placed.

Small clean-ups to fold in: grid_centres (render.rs) duplicates cell_pixel (analysis/overlay.rs) without its edge clamp; add Region::EMPTY, Region::whole(stage) and Segment::stage() to replace the ad hoc region and stage literals scattered through render/, mask_field.rs and proxy.rs; the LayerInput enum plus the MaskInputPixel trait (analysis/mask_overlay.rs) have one production implementer and can become one generic impl; analysis.rs's reduction has five entry points (reduce, reduce_cancellable, reduce_raster, reduce_raster_cancellable, reduce_with_threshold) where reduce_cancellable has no caller outside the file; source validation and check_resamples each run twice across render/entry.rs and render/pipeline.rs; LinearRows::load zero-fills its row buffer on every chunk although load overwrites every element; and docs/design/architecture.md's 'Rendering and limits' section says a pool worker allocates its scratch once and reuses it, where try_for_each_init actually calls init once per Rayon split, typically tens of times per pass.
No behaviour change: this is a mechanical split plus the listed deduplication, proven by an unchanged test suite and byte-identical renders.

tasks.description: Present viewport regions in a separately bounded surface slot and draw generation-matched clipping overlays without exposing stale pixels.
extra_context: Desktop owns app/UI presentation. Retain the full-image slot for settled pans and full-resolution analysis; use bounded front/back region tile sets for viewport frames. Include submitted-but-not-retired allocations, retire GPU resources asynchronously, and hide uncovered or stale texels. Overlay clipping uses the accepted viewport-bounded OR grid and region/content/quality identity; whole-image counts remain marked updating until a matching full report.

Current-view source filtering, readiness before capture, and suppression of an older overlay under any later overlapping region with a different content, generation or quality identity are implemented. The missing older overlay remains hidden until a matching grid arrives, so it never claims pixels from a different displayed region. Focused UI and surface tests pass; post-review quick and rendered checks pass, with 16 targeted timing cases recorded. No post-review full-tier run is claimed.

tasks.description: Measure and bound GPU resources excluded from the provisional 1088 MiB photo-texture ceiling before making a total-memory guarantee.
extra_context: The owner provisionally accepted the 1088 MiB temporary-overlap ceiling on 2026-09-27 for the photo surface slots alone: one current and one retiring full-photo allocation up to 512 MiB each, and two region sets up to 32 MiB each. This is an engineering ceiling, not a total editor or GPU budget.

Crop GPU textures and tile aprons, overlays and backend-owned upload staging are outside that accounting. The core 512 MiB crop raster limit does not itself bound crop GPU residency. The existing backend staging cost is unmeasured. Use representative 24 MP and 60 MP workflows and native M4 GPU evidence, including temporary overlap and retirement, before proposing a total bound.
